newsitem.title: EGYPT: PLO, Israel set initial work plan for negotiations.
newsitem.headline: PLO, Israel set initial work plan for negotiations.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinians set a tentative work plan late on Wednesday night for negotiations on implementing an Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.

"We discussed the agenda. We decided that the security and civilian committees will meet together tonight and then a meeting of the leadership of the steering committee will start tomorrow to finalise the agenda," Palestinian negotiator Jamil Tarifi told Reuters.
Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) and Israeli negotiators resumed formal talks on Wednesday night at the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Taba.
The talks were due to begin at 1500 GMT but Israel asked for a delay. Its team arrived at 2000 GMT. Palestinian negotiators and U.S. mediator Dennis Ross were already at the resort.
The U.S.-sponsored talks are in their second week. The decision to hold them was taken at a Washington summit after clashes last month that killed 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.

The Hebron redeployment was set for March but was delayed by the Israeli government after Islamic suicide attacks killed 59 people in Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu froze the accord when he took office in June, demanding enhanced security for 400 Jewish settlers who live in Hebron amid 100,000 Palestinians.
